title: on-deploy
description: the doftiles deployment orchestrator: verifies the WM-stack binaries, installs the missing ones through per-distro deploy scripts, runs the make install assurances (bun, postinstall trust, the herbctl binary), deploys the dependencies, and provisions the session stack from declarative profiles.

content.heading: on-deploy - the deployment orchestrator
content: **on-deploy** turns the dotfiles repo into a one-command deployment. it runs inside the **doftiles** checkout and reads the deployment manifests:
**wm.required** - required binaries, the deployment model and the deploy target
**stows.required** - the stow packages
**system.required** - each submodule with its dots-relative paths - the scope of the depends walk
**services.required** - the unit order
all four are configurable through configure (tui or flags).
[https://github.com/akinevz2/on-deploy](https://github.com/akinevz2/on-deploy)

content.heading: the verbs
content: `install` / `check` - the requirement walk: resolve every missing binary per <target>.deploy, confirm, run with the tty unlocked (sudo prompts visible), print the command before running it, re-verify. check reports and exits 1 on missing (--json).

`deploy` - install every missing binary: resolve the package, show the command, confirm (Enter = yes), run it, then re-verify - a binary still missing after its command fails the run. `--yes` for non-interactive runs, `--dry-run` to preview.
`services` - the service.order (services.required) runner: check/start/stop/restart/status over the systemd user units, --no-block, stow-safe disable.
`detect-server` - the reachable-X probe (localhost:0.0 style): `--persist-to-systemd` writes DISPLAY into the manager env, `--persist-to-env` writes an rc.d-includable file.

`toolchain` - the make install assurances: bun through npm when missing, trust of the global bun packages' postinstall scripts, the herbctl binary built from the submodule checkout when missing. these used to be four separate makefile recipes (bun-toolchain, bun-trust, on-deploy-ensure, herbctl-ensure) - they are steps of one command now.

`depends` - the per-package walk over system.required: every listed package runs dots/<pkg>/.local/state/depends/<pkg>.makefile (toolchain/build/link/install); `--only` narrows, `--build` for sync+build.

`snapshot` - collect a machine's pre-existing config into doftiles' defaults/ (a stow-shaped package) before the first deploy overwrites it - the machine's prior state, versioned in git, restorable with one make target.
`configure` - edit the deploy target and the required-package list from an interactive menu (or `--target`/`--add`/`--remove` flags).

content.heading: the profiles
content: four session models, co-installable where it makes sense:

`wsl-systemd` - no display manager: hlwm runs as the systemd user unit herbst.service, waiting for the Windows-side X server (VcXsrv) to be reachable. the historical bypass; provision even checks the Windows partition for VcXsrv and offers a silent install from the SourceForge feed.

`nested` - hlwm inside an Xvfb framebuffer, shared over VNC (:5900) and browser noVNC (:6080), with an RDP surface layered on top (xrdp's Xvnc module attaches to the same framebuffer; 3389 stays free for the Windows side). the temporary profile, additive to a primary one.
`xinit` - startx runs ~/.xinitrc; no display manager.
`greetd` - greetd + tuigreet own the console (the bare-OS target).
a profile declares units (systemd user units, enabled additively) and env overrides (written to ~/.config/doftiles/env, read by the units via EnvironmentFile).
the make deploy tui selects the session model, the features, the units and the env - and writes deploy.profile before stowing anything.

content.heading: built to not hang, not lie
content: non-interactive runs abort cleanly demanding --yes instead of blocking on prompts; every install is re-verified; a failed install fails the run.
the prompts ride a raw line reader (bun's readline wedges), and the menu works scripted or interactive.
the deploy script contract is `<target>.deploy <binary>` → the providing package, `install <binary>` → the install command - the resolver per distro, not a package list.

content.heading: herbctl - the binary the toolchain step builds
polyframes - the artifact the deps step deploys
